landings.name: Sugar Creek DNR Public Fishing Area
Deer's Mill Covered Bridge access (SR 234, Shades SP)
Brush Creek access (Narrows Covered Bridge, Turkey Run SP)

corrections.note: Mileage correction: Crawfordsville to Cox Ford (Turkey Run) is ~29 river mi; ~15 mi matches only Crawfordsville-Deer's Mill (15.7). CRITICAL low-head dam at Crawfordsville - put in at the public access below it. Covered bridges: Deer's Mill, Narrows, Cox Ford, West Union. Best spring-early summer; scrapey by late summer. Outfitter URL note: clementscanoes.com domain has lapsed - live site is clementscanoes.net (bases at Crawfordsville and Deer's Mill).

extend_upstream.desc: Tippecanoe River State Park boat launch

landings.name: Tippecanoe River State Park boat launch
Winamac Boat Launch (state public access ramp)

corrections.note: Extent correction: Winamac-Monticello is far more than 20 river mi and ends in Lake Shafer/Freeman reservoir backwater with dams at Monticello - not a day float. Recommended run: Tippecanoe River SP to Winamac Town Park, ~12 mi (the local livery's standard 5-6 hr float); truncate the downstream endpoint at Winamac (41.0514,-86.6031); optional ~7-mi extension to Pulaski Conservation Club. SP coordinate is the park location, not the exact ramp. Hazards: logjams/strainers, not dams, on this stretch; canoe camping available in the state park.

landings.name: Blue River Chapel DNR access (Harrison-Crawford SF)

corrections.note: Mileage correction: Fredericksburg (RM 57) to Milltown (RM 33.5) alone is ~23 mi; Milltown to Rothrock Mill adds ~14 (Cave Country's full-day trip) - ~37 mi total. CRITICAL: dangerous dam at Milltown, portage right; partially breached dam at Rothrock's Mill/White Cloud also requires portage. 'Wyandotte caves country' is the Blue River Chapel reach (RM 11) well below Milltown. Indiana's first Natural & Scenic River; late-summer low water common.

landings.name: Brookville Dam tailwater access (below spillway, off SR 101)
Brookville town access (town park below US 52 bridge)

corrections.note: Mileage correction: Brookville Dam to Harrison OH is ~16-18 river mi, not 12 (AW reach 4688 covers dam to West Fork confluence, 2 mi Class I-III; shorter canonical liveried run is Brookville-New Trenton). Swiftest gradient in Indiana (~6 ft/mi) confirmed. Hazards: keeper hole at the rapid above the US 52 bridge at high dam releases; cold fluctuating tailwater - stay well below the spillway; banks mostly private; no low-head dams on this stretch. Whitewater Canoe Rental (whitewatercanoerental.com) also serves Brookville-New Trenton-Cedar Grove. No source-published coordinates found for these landings - pin manually at named bridges/parks.

extend_downstream.desc: Wildcat Creek Park, Eisenhower Rd, Lafayette (replace Lafayette generic end)

landings.name: Adams Mill access (DNR fishing area at covered bridge)
Davis Ferry Park (Wabash River, below Wildcat mouth)

corrections.note: Extent correction: full Kokomo-Lafayette is 45+ river mi, not 12. Recommended canonical run: Adams Mill to Wildcat Creek Park, ~27 mi; popular day floats are Mis-So-La to Wildcat Park (4.5 mi) and Wildcat Park to Davis Ferry (10 mi). Hazards: old mill dam at Adams Mill (portage, separate accesses above/below); frequent logjams/strainers; Kokomo Reservoir dam upstream. Livery (verified) is at 1850 N 725 E beside the Mis-So-La access, serving this exact stretch. Caveat: Tippecanoe County ended its Wildcat Creek Park lease in 2022 - the DNR site remains a listed access but confirm current status.

landings.name: Rainsville Bridge put-in (CR 25 E, gauge marks on pier)
Twin Bridges access (Twin Bridges Rd off SR 55)
Ouabache Park on the Wabash (0.7 mi below Big Pine mouth)

corrections.note: Extent confirmed: Rainsville bridge to Twin Bridges, 6.7 mi per American Whitewater - Class II-II+ (III high water): Rocky Ford ledges, S-Curve (nasty hole above ~4 ft on the Rainsville gauge), All Day Wave. Strictly seasonal (~400-500 cfs, mainly March-May); usually too low in summer. No dams; hazards are strainers in rapids and private banks. Optional 7-mi Class I continuation Twin Bridges to Ouabache Park, Attica. No livery serves Big Pine - self-shuttle only.

extend_upstream.desc: Owens Bend County Park (correct upstream endpoint, NE of Columbus)

extend_downstream.desc: Mill Race Park, Columbus (Flatrock/Driftwood confluence forming East Fork White; replaces erroneous Edinburgh endpoint)

corrections.note: DIRECTION FIX: the Flatrock flows SOUTHWEST from the Rushville/St. Paul area down TO Columbus, joining the Driftwood at Mill Race Park to form the East Fork White River - it never reaches Edinburgh. Recommended run: Owens Bend to Mill Race Park (~9 mi, approx from the outfitter's 5-hr trip). Hazard: low-head dam between Owens Bend and Mill Race (near Noblitt Park) - portage required (confirmed by Pathfinder trip page); frequent strainers; usually too low by August. Pathfinder (verified) runs shuttle-only on the Flatrock, no rentals. Longer option: SR 252/Flat Rock or SR 9 access to Columbus ~23 mi; upstream Class I-II play stretch Old US 421 to Conn's Creek at St. Paul (AW reach 4173, 6.8 mi).

landings.name: Driftwood public fishing area (Atterbury FWA, off US 31)
Lowell Bridge public access (CR 325W at Lowell Rd)

corrections.note: Direction as mapped (Edinburgh south to Columbus) is CORRECT: the Driftwood forms 1 mi west of Edinburgh at the Big Blue/Sugar Creek confluence and joins the Flatrock at Mill Race Park to form the East Fork White. Mileage correction: full Atterbury-to-Mill Race run is ~15.5-16 river mi, not 8. No dams; fast current through Atterbury FWA woods, watch strainers. Blue's Canoe Livery (Edinburgh) runs Driftwood trips (7-9 mi segments); Pathfinder Outfitters (Columbus) also serves it.

Mileage flag: Columbia City-North Manchester-Logansport is the FULL Eel River Water Trail, ~90 mi, not 15 (South Whitley-Logansport alone ~70-78). For a ~15-mi highlight use North Manchester (Warvel Park) to Stockdale. CRITICAL low-head dams upstream-to-downstream: Collamer (portage left), Liberty Mills (portage right), North Manchester, Stockdale Mill at Roann (~200-yd portage; use access east of town), Chili (scout), Mexico (reported breached - verify), plus Logansport dams below Riverside Park - take out at Riverside/Spencer Park. No current outfitter: Ride the Eel (North Manchester) closed in early 2025.

extend_upstream.desc: Cook's Landing County Park, Huntertown (replace Auburn start - creek above is too shallow/logjammed; CR 35 N of Auburn is high-water only)

extend_downstream.desc: SR 1 DNR access, Leo-Cedarville - last Cedar Creek take-out ~0.9 mi above the St. Joseph confluence

landings.name: Metea County Park (Hursh Rd bridge, 300-yd carry)
Shoaff Park ramp (St. Joseph River continuation)

corrections.note: Lower 13.7 mi is a state Natural, Scenic & Recreational river through Cedar Creek Canyon (Metea County Park, ACRES preserves). Shifting logjams/strainers; best spring/fall higher water. Cedarville Dam sits on the St. Joseph immediately UPSTREAM of the Cedar Creek mouth - no portage for creek paddlers, but stay clear of the dam outflow at the confluence. St. Joe continuation from SR 1: Shoaff Park 9.6 mi. Outfitter is the Fort Wayne-area livery (listed by NEI Water Trails); Cedar Creek itself is self-shuttle. Data flag: NEI's printed Tonkel Rd coordinate duplicates the SR 1 longitude (likely misprint) - pin Tonkel manually at the bridge.

extend_upstream.desc: Mississinewa Dam tailwater access, Fire Ln (replace Marion start - the reservoir and 140-ft dam separate Marion from the Peru tailwater)

landings.name: Gas City Park launch (South H St)
CR 500 N bridge (last take-out above Mississinewa Lake)
Mississinewa Dam tailwater access (Fire Ln, DNR ramp)

corrections.note: Extent correction: 'Marion to tailwater near Peru' is not one run - Mississinewa Lake (USACE) and its 140-ft dam sit between, and the dam is not portage-friendly. Recommended classic float is the NEI 'Seven Pillars' run: dam tailwater (Fire Ln) to SR 124 at Peru, 5.3 mi, passing the Seven Pillars limestone bluffs ~2 mi below the dam. NO public landing at Seven Pillars (ACRES Land Trust: access is private, barriers in place) - view from the water. Tailwater fluctuates with dam releases - check USACE discharge. Upper alternative: Matthews/Gas City/Marion to CR 500 N at Jalapa above the lake, with low-head dam portages near Matthews and Charles Mill Park.
